technical.prompt: What is a multi-strategy hedge fund?
expectedPoints: One fund running many strategies or trading teams
Aims for steady returns with low correlation

choices.answer: One fund allocating capital across many strategies and trading teams
distractors: A fund that follows one strategy in several countries
A fund that invests in other hedge funds only
A fund that changes its single strategy each year

technical.prompt: What is a pod in a multi-strategy fund?
expectedPoints: A small team run by a portfolio manager

choices.answer: A small team with its own capital and strategy under firm risk limits
distractors: A separate legal fund for each investor
A trading desk that serves outside clients
A group of analysts who only write research

technical.prompt: What is a drawdown stop-out in a multi-strategy fund?
expectedPoints: A rule cutting a pod's capital after losses
Often a partial cut at one level and full stop at another

choices.answer: A rule that cuts or removes a pod's capital after set losses
distractors: A rule that doubles a pod's capital after losses
A limit on how many trades a pod can make
A fee charged to pods for trading

technical.prompt: How are portfolio managers at multi-strategy funds typically paid?
expectedPoints: A share of their own pod's profits

choices.answer: A share of their own pod's profits
distractors: A fixed salary with no link to results
A share of the whole firm's management fees only
A percentage of assets under management

technical.prompt: What are pass-through expenses?
expectedPoints: Costs charged directly to fund investors
Such as trader pay, data and technology
Often in place of a fixed management fee

choices.answer: Costs such as trader pay charged directly to investors
distractors: Taxes paid by the fund on behalf of investors
Fees refunded to investors when returns are low
Costs paid by the fund manager personally

technical.prompt: Why do multi-strategy funds use central risk management?

choices.answer: To monitor total exposure and overlaps across all pods
distractors: To pick every stock the pods trade
To market the fund to new investors
To set the pay of every employee

technical.prompt: Why do investors value multi-strategy funds?

choices.answer: Diversified returns with lower volatility and strong risk control
distractors: They guarantee a positive return in every month
They charge the lowest fees in the industry
They invest only in short-term government bonds

technical.prompt: Why do multi-strategy funds usually target market-neutral pods?
expectedPoints: Returns from skill, not market direction
Central book handles any market exposure

choices.answer: So returns come from skill and pods combine without adding market risk
distractors: Market-neutral pods are guaranteed to make a profit
Regulators ban multi-strategy funds from market exposure
Market-neutral pods can run without any capital

technical.prompt: Why do multi-strategy funds often use significant leverage?
expectedPoints: Individual pod returns are small and hedged
Leverage scales them to attractive fund returns
Relies on diversification and risk controls

choices.answer: To scale small, hedged pod returns into attractive fund returns
distractors: Leverage removes all risk from the fund
Regulators require high leverage
Leverage lowers the fund's costs

technical.prompt: How does a multi-strategy fund decide how much capital to give each pod?

choices.answer: Risk-adjusted track record, capacity, correlation and opportunity
distractors: Equal capital to every pod regardless of results
Capital based on each manager's years of age
Capital set by the fund's largest investor

technical.prompt: Why is recruiting portfolio managers so important for multi-strategy funds?
expectedPoints: Returns depend on the talent in the pods

choices.answer: Returns depend on proven managers, who are in high demand
distractors: Recruiting has no real effect on the fund's returns
Portfolio managers are assigned to funds by regulators
Platforms hire only recent graduates as managers

technical.prompt: What is a central risk book?
expectedPoints: Positions held centrally by the fund

choices.answer: Centrally held positions that hedge or adjust total fund exposure
distractors: A record of every investor's account and balance
A written book of trading rules for the pods
A risk report that is sent to regulators each year

technical.prompt: Why do multi-strategy funds often have long investor lock-ups?

choices.answer: To keep capital stable for leveraged strategies
distractors: Regulators require ten-year lock-ups
Investors prefer never withdrawing

technical.prompt: What is crowding risk in multi-strategy platforms?

Stop-outs trigger selling across the industry

choices.answer: Similar positions across pods and funds unwinding at once
distractors: Too many people in the office
Too many investors in the fund
Too many trades on one exchange

technical.prompt: What types of strategies do multi-strategy funds typically combine?
expectedPoints: Macro and fixed income relative value

choices.answer: Equity long/short, macro, quant, credit and event-driven
distractors: Only long-only equity funds that track an index
Only short-dated government bond funds
Only real estate development and construction

technical.prompt: What is the netting problem in multi-strategy pay?
expectedPoints: Winning pods are paid even if others lose
Fund may pay out more than its net profit justifies
Costs fall on investors through pass-through fees

choices.answer: Winning pods are paid even when losing pods cancel the firm's profit
distractors: Pods must share all losses and profits equally
Managers must repay the fund for their pod's losses
Nobody is paid if any single pod loses money

technical.prompt: Why do multi-strategy funds monitor factor exposure across pods?
expectedPoints: Pods may unknowingly share factor bets
Factor moves can hit many pods at once

choices.answer: Pods may share hidden factor bets that hit many at once
distractors: Factors only affect one pod at a time
Factor exposure is always zero
Factors set the pods' pay

technical.prompt: What infrastructure does a multi-strategy platform need?

choices.answer: Risk systems, data, execution, compliance and talent management
distractors: Only a single trading screen for all pods
Only a marketing team and a website
Only office space in a financial centre

technical.prompt: Why might a multi-strategy fund prefer steady returns over high but volatile ones?
